item.text: {"question_id":"5B.5","answer":"For the 2023 period, the evidence shows some government enforcement and reform commitments, but not consistent resistance to politically connected privilege. The government reported monitoring recruitment firms and revoking 112 licences, and the NTRA imposed a 20 million EGP fine on Telecom Egypt; these are concrete, ruler-attributed enforcement actions, although the supplied records do not establish the grounds, independence, or broader deterrent effect of the licence revocations and do not show that the regulator was independent (BATCH-0009-R04-E005; BATCH-0002-E035). Egypt also announced publication of state-owned-enterprise accounts and large procurement contracts under the IMF programme, and approved proposals concerning regulator independence and state-company governance, but these were commitments or proposed measures whose full implementation is not established (BATCH-0022-E014; BATCH-0006-E021). Against this limited counterweight, the evidence describes the anticorruption authority controlled by Sisi as lacking credibility, transparency, and impartiality and unable to monitor military economic activity; military-company allocations and large-SOE audits were not publicly disclosed (BATCH-0002-E004; BATCH-0002-E005). Military-managed civilian projects retained substantial autonomy over licensing, partner selection, and subcontracting, with inaccessible project and financial data and no hard evidence of effective compliance monitoring (BATCH-0009-R10-E002; BATCH-0009-R10-E004). The record further reports no-bid contracts benefiting the military and regime-connected actors, privileged access for major and Gulf investors, and marginalization of small farmers (BATCH-0005-E010; BATCH-0009-R11-E001). Although the government announced a plan to sell shares in 32 state-owned enterprises, including two military-run companies, the sale of military companies was repeatedly postponed; new land was allocated to the army in early 2023, and the analysis describes military veto power and continuing reluctance to reevaluate its economic role (BATCH-0009-R11-E009; BATCH-0009-R11-E010; BATCH-0009-R11-E011). Thus, the evidence supports limited and sector-specific enforcement alongside substantial opacity, privileged access, weak independent oversight, and non-remedy of military-connected economic capture; it does not establish that every reported favoritism allegation was adjudicated or quantify its fiscal effects.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-R04-E005","BATCH-0002-E035","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0006-E021"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0009-R10-E002","BATCH-0009-R10-E004","BATCH-0005-E010","BATCH-0009-R11-E001","BATCH-0009-R11-E009","BATCH-0009-R11-E010","BATCH-0009-R11-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The licence-revocation record does not state the grounds, timing, independence, or remedies, and the Telecom Egypt fine does not establish broader regulator independence.","Disclosure, governance, regulator-independence, and privatization measures are partly commitments or plans; full compliance and completed implementation are not established.","Much adverse evidence is analytical or institutional rather than based on disclosed contract-level adjudications, audits, or court findings.","The supplied evidence does not identify all beneficiaries or quantify the fiscal effects of favoritism or capture."],"corrections_made":["Recast anti-corruption strategies, IMF transparency requirements, and governance measures as commitments or proposals unless implementation was directly shown.","Added the reported recruitment-firm monitoring and 112 licence revocations as a qualified enforcement counterweight.","Integrated the planned sale of 32 state-owned enterprises, repeated postponement of military-company privatization, early-2023 army land allocation, and military veto-power evidence.","Removed any implication that licence revocations necessarily reflected proven non-compliance or that the Telecom Egypt fine demonstrated systemic enforcement."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
